references.text: Psalm 39:5 also points to human frailty and the limited ability to extend one's life, which is similar to the futility of worry in Matthew 6:27.
Isaiah 40:6-8 speaks of human transience in contrast to God's eternal word, which can be seen as related to the theme in Matthew 6:27 about humanity's limited control over their own life.
Proverbs 27:1 warns against boasting about tomorrow, which can be linked to the idea in Matthew 6:27 of not worrying about the future.
Philippians 4:6 encourages believers not to be anxious but instead to bring their requests to God, echoing the message in Matthew 6:27 about not worrying.
James 4:14 reflects on how short and uncertain life is, which can be seen in connection with the question of the futility of worry in Matthew 6:27.
